name: Far-right politics
summary: Far-right politics sits to the right of the mainstream right and combines ultranationalism, nativism, authoritarian law-and-order politics and, in its populist form, hostility to elites and supranational bodies. It pictures the nation as a homogeneous organic community threatened by immigration, diversity and liberal pluralism, and defends traditional family, gender and cultural values. Its economics is not fixed: parties mix welfare for natives only (welfare chauvinism), protectionism and market liberalism.
scope: The contemporary Western populist radical right as described by Mudde and Minkenberg, and documented in the AfD basic programme (2017 English edition), with the extreme right (neo-fascism, neo-Nazism, white-nationalist and conspiracist fringes) noted as a more revolutionary and more violence-tolerant strand. Excludes historical interwar fascism as a program, and non-Western far-right regimes and parties whose nativism is not central. Many economic and institutional questions are left at low confidence because the strands diverge.

keyFigures.name: Julius Evola
keyFigures.role: Italian Traditionalist thinker named in the Wikipedia article as an influence on Bannon and Dugin.

keyFigures.name: Renaud Camus
keyFigures.role: French author who originated the Great Replacement thesis of white Europeans being replaced.

keyFigures.name: Marine Le Pen
keyFigures.role: Leader of France's National Rally, cited as a prominent far-right politician embracing the replacement narrative.

sources.usedFor: The replacement conspiracy theory, its originator and its spread among far-right politicians.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Radical right parties accept state healthcare for natives (welfare chauvinism) while US-style far right opposes it, so adherents split; inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The AfD programme keeps minimum wages to stop profit privatisation, but no strand campaigns for a substantial rise; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sources say far-right economics ranges from free-market to corporatist and welfare-state positions, so there is no single answer.

public-ownership.rationale: Mudde's socioeconomic element includes state control of certain sectors, but broad public ownership of utilities is not a staple; inferred lean against.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The AfD programme abolishes wealth and inheritance taxes and caps taxation; populists attack elites rhetorically but rarely propose higher wealth taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Far-right movements historically opposed independent unions, though blue-collar voters are a base; inferred from the anti-egalitarian, organicist outlook.

property-fundamental.rationale: AfD stresses limiting state access to citizens' assets; organicism lets the nation override property in some strands, hence only mild support.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-globalist rhetoric attacks multinationals while the AfD seeks deregulation and less bureaucracy; adherents split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare chauvinism keeps welfare for natives rather than cutting it, though work-conditioned in AfD text; inferred lean against general cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is a left-wing idea opposed by a radical anti-communist, organicist right that favours class collaboration.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Law and order and security are core far-right themes, so surveillance against terrorism fits; the statement is not directly discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Traditional values and law-and-order stances lead the far right to oppose legalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The AfD programme denounces political correctness and banned terms around immigration and demands tolerance of criticism of Islam, so legal speech limits are rejected.

strong-leader.rationale: Mudde's framework lists a cult of personality and hierarchism; radical-right populists favour decisive leaders though many keep electoral limits.

state-harmful.rationale: The far right is statist about order, borders and the nation, so declaring the state itself harmful is foreign to it.

limit-guns.rationale: The AfD programme opposes tightening firearms law as punishing law-abiding citizens; European strands are less uniform than the US right.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law and order is part of the contemporary far-right definition and the AfD programme calls for strengthening the armed forces and policing.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Traditional-values orientation suggests opposition, but the sources do not address it directly; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The far right is nation-centred and wants the nation-state empowered against Brussels, though AfD invokes subsidiarity against the EU; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Law-and-order emphasis favours punishment and deterrence over rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: The AfD programme has a chapter committing to the traditional family and criticising state day-care and gender mainstreaming for undermining it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Traditional family and gender roles are core to the radical right and the AfD defines family as the traditional unit, though some West European parties are accommodating.

abortion-legal.rationale: The AfD programme welcomes unborn children and criticises the roughly 100,000 abortions for social reasons; European far-right parties vary on legal bans.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religious nationalism and Christian identity recur, but many parties are secular and use Christianity as culture; mixed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Exclusivism, ethnocentrism and antiegalitarianism make active redress for historical racial injustice unwelcome.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The AfD programme ends funding of gender research and gender mainstreaming and treats gender roles as natural.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving a culturally homogeneous community is the core theme; the AfD programme asserts a dominant national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Reactionary strands defend tradition while the extreme right is revolutionary; adherents split on pace.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anti-immigration politics is the centre of Western European far-right parties and the AfD programme calls for sharply restricting and reversing immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposition to globalism and supranational bodies is central; the AfD accepts the UN only as a limited forum.

free-trade.rationale: The AfD programme rejects TTIP, CETA and TiSA; economic nationalism is typical.

nation-first.rationale: Putting the own group first is the heart of far-right nationalism; the AfD wants foreign policy committed to German interests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The AfD foreign policy is framed around national security and economic interests and non-interference, not human-rights wars.

open-borders.rationale: Border control and anti-immigration politics are central; open borders is the opposite of their programme.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits on growth are not advanced; AfD opposes climate policy that burdens the economy; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The AfD programme calls German climate policy a fallacy and says CO2 is not a harmful substance; Wikipedia notes rejection of environmentalism as backlash.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The radical right uses modern technology but traditionalism is wary of progress narratives; no stated position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The AfD programme grants lifetime extensions to nuclear plants while exploring alternatives, a weak pro-nuclear lean.

revolution-justified.rationale: De Jonge's split: the extreme right is revolutionary while the radical right is reformist and electoral.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anti-establishment populism distrusts experts and elites; the AfD wants Swiss-style referenda.

central-planning.rationale: Corporatist state control of some sectors is typical but a fully planned economy is rejected as communist.

socialized-markets.rationale: Worker or public ownership is not a far-right position; inferred from anti-communism.

land-value-tax.rationale: The AfD wants lower taxes and fewer duties; a land-value tax is not discussed; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The AfD programme explicitly abolishes wealth and inheritance taxes and favours family wealth transfer.

basic-income.rationale: The AfD offers only a work-enabling basic income and compensation for parents, not an unconditional one.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism and protectionism against globalisation are common, though free-market strands exist.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mudde lists state control of certain sectors in the far-right socioeconomic programme; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Agrarianism and a small-business and artisan base suggest sympathy; not stated as a programme.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Radical anti-communism rejects abolition of money and wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The AfD criticises the euro and ECB but wants national currencies, not no central banks; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism is in Mudde's far-right socioeconomic list, but contemporary parties rarely advance it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Fascist and extreme-right strands accept one-party rule, but the mainstream radical right competes in elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Reactionary strands favour monarchy while others do not; the sources give no consensus.

democracy-best.rationale: Scholars describe the far right as opposed to liberal democracy, favouring illiberal or ethnocratic forms.

direct-votes.rationale: The AfD programme states the German people should vote on laws made by parliament, and populist radical right parties champion referenda.

workers-councils.rationale: Council democracy is a left-socialist idea alien to hierarchical, anti-communist far right.

right-to-secede.rationale: Unitary nationalism opposes secession, though ethnic separatists favour it; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hierarchism and the idea of a superior minority leading appear in descriptions of the far right.

political-violence-never.rationale: The extreme right condones violence while the radical right rejects it; adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Palingenetic fascist strands glorify war, but modern radical-right parties do not; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religious identity is bound to the nation in many strands; others are secular; weak lean.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A theocratic minority exists, but most far-right parties use religion as culture, not law; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Law and order and a strong state make privatised courts and defence alien.

military-superiority.rationale: The AfD programme wants a strengthened armed force and compulsory service; nationalist posture fits.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Both sources describe an ethnically or culturally homogeneous nation as the central idea.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Organicism treats society as one unified body and replaces class struggle with national struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Miller-Idriss, cited in the Wikipedia article, calls the far right antiegalitarian.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed; the far right defends the established nation-state and its settler majority; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Chauvinism and defence of national history make reparations unacceptable.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some groups favour a Christian Europe while the AfD wants a Europe of nation states; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Non-individualist, organicist thinking subordinates individual interest to the community.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Mudde includes non-individualist traits and law and order; duties to the national community come first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Mudde notes protection of the natural environment as a traditional reference, and the AfD programme speaks of unspoilt nature; weak.

limit-population.rationale: The AfD favours pronatalism for natives and sees a demographic crisis, so active limits are rejected domestically.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The radical right embraces modern technology and economic strength, though traditionalists lament modernity; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Accelerationism exists as a fringe aimed at violent collapse, not tech; the mainstream is traditionalist.

human-enhancement.rationale: Traditionalism and religious conservatism suggest wariness; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not discussed; the populist emphasis on popular votes and national leaders suggests rejection; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Law-and-order and security priorities lean toward state access; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The article lists a Golden Age myth and reactionary conservatism as defining archetypes of far-right politics.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Far-right movements are ideologically driven around purity and nation; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Radical right parties follow electoral routes, while extreme-right fringes use direct action; mild lean against.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources document no stance on whether methods should prefigure ends; the extreme right accepts violence while the radical right is electoral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The far right values national strength and uses modern technology; primitivism is not part of it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchism and a corporatist social order reject it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Anti-egalitarian and anti-communist; distribution by need is communist.

production-for-use.rationale: Some revolutionary-right strands are anti-capitalist, but production for use is communist; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Class collaboration and anti-communism reject the exploitation thesis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Radical anti-communism is one of the four core features given in the Wikipedia definition.

collective-farming.rationale: Agrarianism favours family farms and the peasantry, not collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a far-right claim; the right blames globalism and elites instead; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Some strands such as the AfD want lower taxes but accept the state; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Traditional values and law and order justify restricting adult conduct beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Organicism and exclusivism assign rights through membership of the national group.

conscription.rationale: The AfD programme explicitly calls for reinstating compulsory military service for men aged 18-25.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not discussed; the far right ties people to the nation and values voting for populist outsiders; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is the guardian of the nation, not a service business; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Free-market and traditional stances do not treat material means as a freedom precondition; mixed.

media-academia-power.rationale: The AfD programme complains of newspeak and political correctness enforced by media; populists attack university-media elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The extreme right has scientific racism while mainstream radical-right parties avoid it; adherents split.

organic-representation.rationale: Organicism and corporatism favour representation through families and bodies, but it is not the mainstream programme.

total-state.rationale: Fascism favoured a total state but the contemporary mainstream does not; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Palingenesis, or national rebirth from decadence, is named as a key far-right myth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Irredentism exists but modern parties are defensive; the AfD programme stresses sovereignty; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal-oath rule is not on the programme; far right favours nation-states.

bound-labor.rationale: Not any modern far-right position; inferred from the agrarian small-owner ideal.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The far right claims objective truth suppressed by political correctness; relativism is not endorsed; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Camus and Lebourg describe a rejection of universalism.

single-common-good.rationale: Mudde's monism holds that the people have a single will and a single good, against pluralism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Many European far-right parties now ally with Israel; antisemitic strands dissent; mixed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ethnic nationalism extends citizenship to co-ethnics, but the statement is not directly addressed; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cultural nationalism usually supports language revival; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Hierarchism and class collaboration oppose democratic control of firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: No documented consensus; inferred split between free-market and statist wings.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The AfD stresses fiscal rectitude and the debt ceiling but other parties spend; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic positions of the far right vary from free-market to corporatist.

rule-by-example.rationale: Law and order approaches rely on laws and punishments; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: The AfD programme asks for the freedom of European nations free of foreign paternalism, and nationalism is the core.

force-without-un.rationale: The AfD wants a UN role in conflicts but other groups want freedom of action; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Traditionalist and religious strands subordinate reason; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare chauvinism is a defining feature in Mudde's definition; the AfD programme conditions benefits on years of contribution by citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The AfD programme stresses making work worthwhile and conditionality of benefits.

class-collaboration.rationale: Organicism and corporatism have employers and workers cooperate in the national body.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The far right values inherited culture and national heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: The Dugin-Evola strand favours it while Western parties prioritise nations; split.

workers-nation.rationale: Blue-collar nationalism is the far-right model; internationalist class organisation is rejected.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Radical right favours traditional gender roles, as the article states.

ban-interest.rationale: Some revolutionary-right strands oppose usury, but it is not the programme; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The far right has exclusivist strands wanting separation, but the mainstream rejects legal racial classification; mild lean against.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Organicism rejects the Marxist view of the state as class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The AfD programme rejects climate policy and renewables subsidies; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The AfD programme asserts a dominant German culture that immigrants must integrate into, and stresses that Islam does not belong to Germany.

elite-replacement.rationale: Many far-right politicians endorse the Great Replacement claim, though not all and scholars reject it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not defining; the AfD supports reforms of election law.

national-mission.rationale: Nationalism tends toward defending the own nation, not exporting its system; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Traditional gender roles, antifeminism and the rejection of gender studies reject this.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-establishment populism against corrupt elites and mainstream parties is a stated core feature.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics lives only in fringe racialist strands; the AfD is pro-natal; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Law-and-order loyalty to police and military; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A strong state in culture, family and security goes beyond a night-watchman role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The extreme right opposes mixing while the mainstream avoids it; split.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hierarchism and the view that some groups should have greater rights contradict it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist doctrinal debate that the far right does not address.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Defence of national history makes labelling the nation colonial unacceptable; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The AfD programme rejects special rights for Muslim pupils and religious law in public life.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Western far-right parties defend individual religious identity against Islam rather than regulating conversion; inferred, with only fringe religious-nationalist dissent.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Western far-right demand; the AfD focuses on halal and kosher slaughter bans instead.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The AfD wants Islamic studies folded into ethics but grounds culture partly in Christianity; split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question not addressed by the far right.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Populist radical right claims popular sovereignty, but the extreme right and ethnocracy limit it.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism favours export strength; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: The AfD programme calls for repatriation and deportations; remigration is a stated aim of identitarian groups.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Law and order and a strong state use force; non-aggression is libertarian.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist hierarchy and struggle between peoples appear in far-right strands; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Far-right parties themselves face bans and oppose them as undemocratic; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This republican concept does not appear in the sources; populist anti-elite rhetoric echoes it while authoritarian traits cut against it.

separated-powers.rationale: De Jonge notes the radical right opposes separation of powers and minority protections.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist concept; the far right has leader-centred parties but no vanguard doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Welfare chauvinism prioritises citizens, not the poor as a class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The radical right appeals to property-owning blue-collar voters and small owners; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Far right is hostile to organised labour militancy; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The AfD links Germany's concern to birth rates and not poverty to population; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Both articles say the far right sees pluralism and diversity as a threat to a homogeneous community.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hierarchism and the idea of a leading minority sit badly with random selection of office-holders, and populists prefer elections and referenda.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian traits of the far right favour strong emergency powers; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic positions range from free-market to state-interventionist across the far right, so there is no shared view on emergency price caps.

party-controls-media.rationale: Far-right parties campaign against media bias; the AfD abolishes broadcasting fees; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Armed forces are loyal to the nation and state not party; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The AfD programme requires multi-year contribution and tightened citizenship rules.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Populist anti-elite rhetoric would back it; AfD seeks lower parliamentary pay; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The sources describe anti-establishment parties that vary from tightly leader-led to loose; no documented doctrine on binding party decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The AfD programme rejects a United States of Europe and wants a Europe of nation states; Euroscepticism is central in Western Europe.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential strongman strands favour it while parliamentary parties do not.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a far-right concern; Christian fundamentalist and national-church strands exist but are not described as taking a side.

clerical-rule.rationale: Theocratic strands exist but are marginal in the far right.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Patriotism and anti-communism reject revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Traditional values support moral limits on art; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Illiberal rulers favour it while parties differ.

recall-officials.rationale: Populist demands for citizen control of politicians; AfD wants to strengthen direct democracy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The AfD keeps NATO as a defensive alliance and seeks stronger armed forces.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not a far-right proposal; property-owner base.

people-in-arms.rationale: The AfD wants conscription and gun rights; replacing the army is not stated.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Blood and soil and agrarianism idealise the countryside.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Ethnic nationalism usually favours reunification of the nation; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-elite populism distrusts the educated and intellectuals; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ethnopluralism says only different, while racialist strands rank cultures; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Law and order favours harsh penalties, though the AfD programme does not endorse capital punishment; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The AfD programme rejects gender mainstreaming and early sexualisation in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian fundamentalist US strands favour it while European parties do not.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The AfD programme states reinstating jus sanguinis as in force until 2000.

minority-language-support.rationale: Exclusivist nationalism favours one national culture.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The AfD programme rejects special rights for Muslims and exemptions for halal and kosher slaughter.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity and homogeneity are valued; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The AfD opposes bailouts and debt mutualisation; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economic nationalists want economic sovereignty but the sources show no demand to transform the property system, so the answer is a split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Neither source discusses constitution-writing procedure; populists favour referenda while the extreme right opposes popular sovereignty.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Authoritarian strands accept it but populist parties defend freedoms; split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The AfD programme limits development aid to capacity building and says migration does not solve poverty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The AfD programme keeps NATO as a defensive alliance and says nothing on a national deterrent, while nationalists elsewhere (such as the French RN) back one.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The AfD programme advocates direct election of the Federal President.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The AfD criticises the ECB and euro and wants accountability; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Organicism subordinates property to the nation but AfD defends private property; split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A dispute among socialists; the far right treats the USSR simply as a communist enemy and does not take a side on its classification.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The AfD programme rejects climate models as hypothetical and opposes precautionary climate policy.

collective-defense.rationale: The AfD programme keeps NATO as a defensive alliance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Defence of annexations varies from irredentist support to condemnation, and the sources record no common line.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: AfD wants Islamic bodies denied public status but not Christian church curbing; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Monarchist and presidential strongman strands disagree, and a symbolic head of state above parties is not a documented far-right demand.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Unitary ethnonationalism usually treats the national territory as indivisible, though ethnic separatists dissent; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; unitary nationalism favours uniformity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A divine-descent ruler belongs to Japanese imperial ideology, not to the Western nativist far right; even the personality cults described are secular.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The AfD wants lower taxes and a ceiling but no flat tax in text opened.

character-from-environment.rationale: Hierarchism and essentialism emphasise innate nature and heredity.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The AfD stresses rule of law and independent courts despite authoritarian traits.

space-expansion.rationale: No source ties far-right politics to a space programme; the question is outside its documented concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The ancient doctrine of mixed rule is not discussed; the hierarchist side favours rule by a few, the populist side rule by the many.

leader-cult.rationale: Cult of personality appears in Mudde's far-right framework.

equal-parenting.rationale: AfD traditional family focus not addressed to custody.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A dispute inside Maoism that the far right does not engage; it rejects socialism entirely so the question has no hold.

land-redistribution.rationale: Defence of property and landowners; Guatemala example reversed agrarian reform.

refugee-return.rationale: The statement concerns Palestinian-style claims which are not addressed; inferred split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentist ethnic nationalism claims territory for co-ethnics in some strands; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Western far right defends individual religious choice vs Islam; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: The AfD programme calls for a ban on full-body veiling and rejects Islamic dress norms.

common-currency.rationale: The AfD programme calls for ending the euro and returning to national currencies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Germanism and pan-European strands favour it but others do not.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Exclusivist nationalism opposes separate institutions for minorities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Nativists would say minorities should not claim equal status while exclusivists urge emigration, but the sources do not record a view on this Zionist-versus-Bundist question.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Idealist and organic nationalism rejects materialist history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporatist strands tolerate concentrated economic organisation while anti-globalist populists attack multinationals; no common position.

no-bailouts.rationale: The AfD programme rejects bailouts and credit guarantees such as for Greece.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populists oppose liberal constraints on majority will; De Jonge notes opposition to rule of law restraints.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The AfD programme calls gender quotas unproductive and unfair.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The AfD rejects most trade agreements; binding standards not addressed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky appears in some historic far-right ideologies but not modern parties.

moral-incentives.rationale: Social duty is emphasised but moral incentive economics is a communist idea.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The extreme right's acceleration is a fringe; the mainstream rejects.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hierarchism and the aim of rule by a superior minority fit with inherited status, and the far right defends tradition against levelling.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The AfD programme asks for teaching centred on the nation's culture and pride.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial paternalism is historic; modern parties avoid.

patriotic-education.rationale: The AfD programme calls for pride in nation and its symbols in schools and criticises schools without pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposition to racial preferences follows from anti-egalitarian exclusivism.

public-money-creation.rationale: The AfD attacks the ECB and euro but wants no state money monopoly; heterodox monetary ideas appear in some strands, so adherents split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not a far-right topic; strands range from anti-capitalist revolutionary right to free-market, so no single judgement on capitalism's crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Russian and Turkish nationalists pursue it while Western nativist parties are inward-looking, so adherents split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Economic nationalism favours protection but not economic withdrawal by poor countries; inferred from anti-globalism applied to the statement.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that the far right does not use; its welfare chauvinism instead defends native workers' entitlements.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian wing agrees; others restrict; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Populists oppose entrenched limits on majority; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; border revisionists favour it for their own nation while defenders of the state order reject it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Monarchist and republican strands both exist among the far right, and the sources give no common answer.

minority-veto.rationale: De Jonge, cited in the article, says the radical right opposes minority rights and protections, so letting a dissenting minority block a decision is rejected.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: No documented stance; populists endorse resisting elites while authoritarians back rulers' prerogatives.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Populists back the elected body against courts, but strongman and monarchist strands reject parliamentary supremacy; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The AfD programme states animals are sentient creatures and bans ritual slaughter without stunning.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The AfD programme accepts agriculture and hunting while stressing animal protection.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchism and organicism imply the elite's duty to the nation; the AfD wants support for families.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Far-right movements stress mobilising and defending the nation against threats, so retreat from public life is not their ideal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Frankfurt-school thesis is not used by the far right, though it blames media and cultural elites for shaping opinion.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Gramscian hegemony thesis is not documented here; the far right has its own cultural-elite narrative but not this one.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim not used by the far right, which attributes poverty to home-country failings; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reservation of jobs and benefits for citizens is stated as a typical demand.

party-own-road.rationale: A dispute inside the communist movement that the far right does not take part in.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The AfD programme says aid should build capacity at home.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist in some strands but not mainstream.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Defence of established national communities rejects.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The far right rejects anti-fascism as left-wing doctrine, and neo-fascist strands identify with fascism, so it cannot be a founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Radical anti-communism treats communism as the main enemy and fascism comparison is rejected by the extreme right but accepted by radical right.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: US-specific historical question not covered; some US far-right neo-Confederates deny slavery's centrality while others do not.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Defence of national heritage; Croatian and Japanese examples.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The article notes the alt-right draws on the manosphere, which campaigns on male disadvantage and rejects feminist priorities.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Manosphere-influenced antifeminism emphasises male victimhood; inferred, since the sources do not discuss this issue directly.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Camus and Lebourg describe the far right's rejection of universalism, which implies different civilisations should keep their own institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Authoritarian strands favour military role; Pinochet example.

paid-care-work.rationale: The AfD wants compensating parents so partly agrees, but not feminist framing.

filial-duty.rationale: Traditional family values are a listed far-right feature, which includes respect for elders and obligations within the family.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not in the sources; hierarchism would accept merit ranking while populists distrust technocratic examinees.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism and protectionism against globalisation are typical radical-right positions, so blocking foreign purchases of strategic firms fits.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The AfD programme defends the traditional family as the foundation of society; inferred, since divorce law itself is not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Council-democracy doctrine not used; populist recall demands are mild support but authoritarian strands reject binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The AfD programme encourages private pension arrangements for MPs but not general reform; split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property tied to blood and soil but not use-based; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The AfD programme complains about parliamentary waste and wants strengthened control, but the sources show no view on the specific budget-approval rule.

single-official-language.rationale: The AfD programme requires German in schools and public life for integration.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nativism and economic nationalism favour keeping national land in national hands; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The far right is antiegalitarian and rejects equality-of-outcome enforcement, treating unequal group outcomes as natural.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Revolutionary-right strands criticise materialism while populist right parties court consumer-voters; no common position.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Support for covert war depends on who the target is; anti-communist strands armed insurgents but nativists oppose foreign adventures.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Russian-aligned far-right currents defend bloc enforcement while Western parties oppose foreign military ventures; no common view.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sovereigntist far-right governments and parties, such as in Hungary, portray foreign-funded NGOs and media as threats; the article details anti-globalist stances.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The AfD programme proposes larger families instead of mass immigration with financial support for parents.

residents-only-property.rationale: Nativism and the preferential treatment of locals suggest support, though the sources do not discuss residency limits specifically.

job-guarantee.rationale: Welfare chauvinism wants jobs for natives, but a general state employer of last resort is not a documented position; split.

democratic-peace.rationale: The far right rejects liberal-democratic universalism and democracy promotion; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Law and order and authoritarianism treat obeying the law as a civic duty.

non-intervention.rationale: The AfD stresses peaceful solutions but defends German interests.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not a far-right question and the movement is not described as taking a side.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Antisemitic conspiracy theories, Islamic takeover are documented core of fringe and counter-jihad.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The AfD programme commits to the traditional family and marriage as the foundation of society.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The AfD demands transparency from officials in some areas but populists also attack leaks; no documented common stance.

informal-organisation.rationale: Far-right movements prize leaders, hierarchy and party organisation, though extreme-right cells exist; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The AfD programme asserts national law and sovereignty over supranational courts.

religious-nation.rationale: Religious nationalism is stated for some but not all.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The tributary-system model is not a far-right idea; nationalists reject deference to others.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Northern League-style regionalists favour it while unitary nationalists oppose; split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Anti-communist, property-owning outlook accepts private belongings; only the common-ownership half is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Radical anti-communism is a defining feature.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Welfare-state radical right and free-market radical right differ over provider mix.

religion-illusion.rationale: The far right treats religion as identity, tradition and a source of national cohesion, including religious nationalism and Christian fundamentalism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Free-market strands agree while revolutionary-right and corporatist strands reject the praise; adherents split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The AfD programme opposes gender mainstreaming and gender quotas, treating the family not the economy as women's basis; antifeminism is typical.

socialized-care.rationale: The AfD programme argues state day-care and full-time schools undermine the family and pays parents to raise children themselves.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The AfD programme opposes gender-neutral language changes and stresses German, but does not ask for purging loanwords; split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous-treaty issue not addressed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing cooperatives resemble leftist utopianism, though agrarian and völkisch communal strands exist; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic nationalism seeks homogeneous national territory, which settlement policies in minority areas serve; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third Positionism and the revolutionary right take that line, while most parliamentary radical right parties are market or welfare-oriented; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Blood-and-soil nationalism ties the people to its historic land, though not all strands extend it into stronger claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial belongs to an extra-parliamentary fringe the article names; mainstream radical-right parties disavow it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional values lean against LGBT rights but Western far-right parties have mostly not sought criminalisation; some Eastern strands differ.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The extreme right and fascist strands favour suppression, but the radical right wins power through elections; mild lean against.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Western far-right parties mostly defend free criticism of Islam, as the AfD programme says; blasphemy law is not their aim.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonialism is historic for the far right and modern parties do not address it; inferred split.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The counter-jihad strand treats Islamic militancy as a threat and rejects Islamic law; this Islamist doctrine is not far-right.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: An Islamist takfiri doctrine opposed by the Western far right and its counter-jihad strands.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Mass participation in workplaces and communities is a leftist notion; populists favour referenda rather than participatory decision-making.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The far right rejects the framework of systemic racism and sexism as left-wing ideology and antiegalitarian.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The AfD programme rejects gender mainstreaming and gender-neutral transformation; traditional gender roles are core.

assisted-dying.rationale: The AfD welcomes unborn and newborn life and family values, and religious traditionalists oppose assisted dying; inferred, not explicit.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The far right sees itself as opposed to the left, and Mudde-style definitions position it on the right even though populists claim to transcend the divide; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-establishment populists attack lobbying elites, but free-market strands defend business; adherents split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The AfD programme states that Islam does not belong to Germany and devotes a section to its tense relationship with the value system, a stance central to European radical-right nativism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the radical right blames immigration and elites for workers' woes rather than the wage relation, and treats work as national duty.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Strands split: religious traditionalists agree, while secular populist radical right parties ground authority in the people or nation.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Split: the Western populist radical right often wants bans on Islamic dress but defends Christian symbols, so answers on neutral state dress vary.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from the radical right's opposition to progressive regulation and gender politics, though the position is not defined.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economics varies across the far right, from welfare chauvinism to market liberalism; the AfD programme endorses a social market economy but other strands do not.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Ultranationalism and law-and-order politics treat strong armed forces as essential to national sovereignty.

rich-first.rationale: Strands diverge on economics, and the position is not part of the core nationalist programme.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Sources show strands split on alignment, with some favouring national sovereignty outside blocs and others aligning with NATO or Russia.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Most of the Western radical right works within elected systems and nationalist republics; monarchist fringes exist but no source endorses it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The AfD programme favours a market economy and says nothing in favour of mutual banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The radical right stresses national sovereignty over supranational bodies, though the AfD itself favours fiscal discipline; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The radical right claims to speak for 'the people' and accepts democratic elections; wealth tests clash with that populism.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The article notes far-right hostility to environmentalism and to feminism, so tying the two together is rejected.

reification.rationale: The idea belongs to Marxist theory, which the far right opposes; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The radical right blames media bias and elites, not wealth ownership, and often has its own wealthy backers; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The AfD programme appeals to the rule of law and a constitutional order, though the extreme right is more willing to rule by decree; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The populist radical right defines the nation ethnically but works within electoral democracy, while the extreme right would limit the vote; strands split.

online-participation.rationale: The AfD programme demands direct democracy and referendums, so online participation fits; the internet itself is not mentioned.

open-government-data.rationale: The AfD programme calls for transparency in government and direct democracy; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The AfD frames Islam as a cultural conflict but proposes no marriage ban, and a secular state is the norm in the programme; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The radical right targets Muslims by policy rather than boycott, while antisemitic fringes do call for them; strands split.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Radical right populism favours referendums and a national will voiced by leaders, not randomly selected assemblies; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Radical right parties defend traditional religious and cultural heritage, so modernizing doctrine is not favoured; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Islam is incompatible with our country's culture and values.
missingStatements.rationale: The AfD programme states that Islam does not belong to Germany and devotes a section to its tense relationship with the value system, a stance central to European radical-right nativism.

missingStatements.text: Human activity is the main cause of current climate change.
missingStatements.rationale: The AfD programme calls German climate policy a fallacy built on hypothetical models and says CO2 is not a harmful substance, and the article notes far-right rejection of environmentalism.
missingStatements.declined: Overlaps drastic-climate-action, which already answers -2 for the far right with the same AfD evidence; a separate factual cause statement adds little.

notes: Strands diverge sharply: the extreme right (neo-fascist, neo-Nazi, white-nationalist) would answer revolution, violence, racial hierarchy, segregation and antisemitic conspiracy items more strongly, while parliamentary radical right parties accept elections and disavow denial. Economic answers are low confidence because parties range from free-market to welfare-chauvinist. AfD text is a stand-in for the European populist mainstream, not for every national party.
